findings.title: LLM or secret API called directly from the browser
findings.message: AI provider called directly from browser code; the key is exposed to every visitor.
findings.why: Calling OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and similar APIs from client code ships the API key to every visitor, who can then run up your bill or abuse the account.
findings.fix: Call the provider from a server route or edge function that holds the key, and have the browser call your own endpoint (with auth and rate limiting).

findings.title: Mass assignment
findings.message: The whole request body is unpacked into a model write.
findings.why: The whole request body is written into a database model, so a user can set fields like `role`, `is_admin` or `credits` by adding them to the request.
findings.fix: Copy only the allowed fields explicitly, or validate with a schema that whitelists fields.

findings.title: Server-side request forgery (SSRF)
findings.message: Request data flows into an outbound HTTP request URL (passed in through the call at server/routers/custom_providers.py:1266).
findings.why: The server fetches a URL chosen by the user, which can reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints (credentials).
findings.fix: Allow-list hosts, block private and link-local IPs after DNS resolution, and do not follow redirects to other hosts.

findings.title: Path traversal
findings.message: Request data flows into a file system path.
findings.why: A user-controlled path reaches the file system, so `../../etc/passwd` style input can read or overwrite any file.
findings.fix: Use `secure_filename` / `path.basename`, resolve the final path and check it is inside the allowed directory.

findings.title: SQL injection
findings.message: Request data flows into a SQL query (passed in through the call at server/routers/market_submissions.py:185).
findings.why: Building SQL with string formatting lets an attacker change the query: read other users' data, bypass login or drop tables.
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries (`cursor.execute("... WHERE id = %s", (id,))`, Prisma `$queryRaw` tagged templates, or the ORM query builder).

findings.title: Possible insecure direct object reference (IDOR)
findings.message: PATCH /credentials/{cred_id} changes a record by id without checking that it belongs to the caller.
findings.why: The handler changes a record by the id in the URL but never compares it with the current user, so any logged-in user can change anyone's data by changing the id.
findings.fix: Scope the query by owner (`where id = ? and user_id = current_user.id`) or check ownership before writing.

findings.title: Database query inside a loop (N+1)
findings.message: Database call runs once per loop iteration.
findings.why: One query per item turns a page with 100 rows into 101 round trips: slow pages, timeouts and database load that grows with your data.
findings.fix: Fetch everything in one query (IN / join / include / select_related / prefetch_related) or batch the writes (createMany, bulk_create, executemany).

findings.title: Money stored as a floating-point number
findings.message: `cost_amount` stores money as a floating-point number.
findings.snippet: cost_amount: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(Float, nullable=True, server_default="0.0")
findings.why: Floats cannot represent most decimal amounts exactly (0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3), so totals, refunds and balances drift by cents.
findings.fix: Store integer cents or use NUMERIC/DECIMAL columns and Decimal types.

findings.title: Database query inside a loop (N+1)
findings.message: Database call `execute()` runs once per loop iteration.
findings.why: One query per item turns a page with 100 rows into 101 round trips: slow pages, timeouts and database load that grows with your data.
findings.fix: Fetch everything in one query (IN / join / include / select_related / prefetch_related) or batch the writes (createMany, bulk_create, executemany).

findings.title: Unbounded agent loop
findings.message: Loop calls a model with no step or budget limit.
findings.why: A `while True` loop that calls a model has no iteration or budget limit, so a confused or injected agent can loop forever and burn tokens.
findings.fix: Add a maximum number of steps and a token or cost budget, and stop when either is reached.

findings.why: Without max tokens a single request (or a prompt-injected loop) can generate very long, expensive responses.
findings.fix: Set max_tokens / max_output_tokens / maxOutputTokens to what the feature actually needs.

findings.title: Retired or deprecated model hardcoded
findings.message: Model `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` was retired on 2025-10-28; the provider recommends `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
findings.why: The provider has retired (or announced the retirement of) this model id, so requests fail or will fail without warning.
findings.fix: Move to a current model and keep the model id in configuration rather than in code.

findings.title: Package imported but not declared as a dependency
findings.message: `volcenginesdkarkruntime` is imported but not declared in the project's Python dependencies.
findings.why: The package is installed on the author's machine but missing from requirements.txt, pyproject.toml or package.json, so a clean install (CI, Docker, production) fails with an import error.
findings.fix: Add the package with a pinned version to the project's dependency file.

findings.title: Outbound HTTP request without a timeout
findings.message: `requests.get()` has no timeout; one slow upstream server can hang this worker forever.
findings.why: `requests` and `urlopen` wait forever by default. One slow or dead upstream API ties up a worker per request until the whole service stops responding.
findings.fix: Always pass a timeout, for example `requests.get(url, timeout=10)`.

findings.title: Upload accepted without a size limit
findings.message: The whole upload is read into memory with no size limit.
findings.snippet: async def upload_style_image(project_name: str, _t: Translator, file: UploadFile = File(...)):
findings.why: Reading an upload with no size limit lets one large request exhaust memory or disk and crash the server.
findings.fix: Set a limit (MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH, multer limits.fileSize, a size check before reading) and stream large files.

findings.title: Focus outline removed
findings.message: The focus outline is removed and no other focus style replaces it.
findings.snippet: className="flex flex-1 flex-col text-foreground no-underline outline-none"
findings.why: `outline: none` with no replacement leaves keyboard users unable to see which control has focus (WCAG 2.4.7).
findings.fix: Keep the outline, or replace it with a visible `:focus-visible` style such as a ring, border or box-shadow.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.message: The final image never switches to a non-root USER.
findings.why: If the app is compromised the attacker is root inside the container, which makes escaping and tampering easier.
findings.fix: Add a non-root user and `USER app` at the end of the Dockerfile.

findings.title: Exception silently swallowed
findings.message: Error is caught and ignored.
findings.why: An empty except/catch hides failures, including failed auth or payment calls, and makes incidents very hard to debug.
findings.fix: Log the error and handle it explicitly, or let it propagate.

findings.title: Same function copied into several files
findings.message: `_fetch_lock` is defined with the same code in lib/material/global_library.py; keep one copy and import it, so a fix in one place reaches every caller.
findings.why: A function with the same name and the same code is defined in more than one file of a package. A fix made in one copy does not reach the others, which then drift apart.
findings.fix: Keep one copy in a shared module and import it everywhere.

findings.title: Destructive action without confirmation
findings.message: `onDelete` runs straight from a click, with no confirmation or undo.
findings.why: A delete or remove that runs on a single click, with no confirmation or undo, loses user data on a misclick.
findings.fix: Ask for confirmation (a dialog), or offer undo for a few seconds before deleting for good.

findings.title: Image without width and height
findings.message: has no width and height, so the page jumps when the image loads.
findings.why: The browser cannot reserve space for an image without dimensions, so the content below jumps when it loads (cumulative layout shift, a Core Web Vital).
findings.fix: Set `width` and `height` (the intrinsic size is enough; CSS can still scale it), or give the image a fixed box with CSS such as `aspect-ratio`.
